what: HealthEquity administers health savings accounts: the tax-advantaged accounts Americans use to pay medical costs. It holds the balances, invests them, and earns fees from employers and interest on the cash.
customers: Employers offering high-deductible health plans, and the employees whose accounts it holds.
money: the largest and most profitable part
interest and fees on account balances held
fees on card spending from the accounts
moat: Accounts stay with the administrator the employer chose, and balances accumulate year after year because unspent money rolls over. The asset base compounds without new sales.
risks: Custodial revenue depends on interest rates and falls when they fall
35 times earnings for a business growing in the low teens
opportunities: A 16.4% net margin and $488M of free cash flow on $1.4B of revenue
Revenue grew from $757M to $1.3B in four years, and account balances keep compounding
Analysts see about 24% upside, with 15 covering the stock
watch: Total custodial assets and the yield earned on them.
